def: A classifier or regressor that predicts from the k training points closest to the query, by vote or average.
A method that does no work at training time beyond storing the data, and does all its computation at prediction time.
A numerical measure of how far apart two feature vectors are, such as the Euclidean distance.
The effect that as the number of features grows, points become far apart and almost equally distant, so local neighbourhoods stop being local.
The probability of a class before looking at any features, usually its frequency in the training data.
The probability of the observed features if a given class were true.
A classifier that combines a class prior with per-feature likelihoods under the assumption that features are independent given the class.
Adding a pseudo-count to every feature count so that no feature-class combination has probability zero.
A function K(x, z) that returns the inner product of two points in a richer feature space without constructing that space.
Rewriting an algorithm so data enters only through kernel evaluations, letting a linear method draw curved boundaries.
The Gaussian similarity exp(-gamma times squared distance), which is 1 for identical points and falls towards 0 as they move apart.
Ridge regression performed in a kernel-defined feature space, with one weight per training point.
A classifier that finds the widest-margin boundary between classes, optionally in a kernel feature space.
The gap between the decision boundary and the nearest training points of each class.
The training points on or inside the margin, which alone determine a support vector machine's boundary.
